title: Building Scalable Systems: Lessons from the Trenches
excerpt: Key principles and patterns for building systems that scale with your business.
author: Stone C. Lasley
content:
Scalability isn't just about handling more users—it's about building systems that can evolve with your business needs. Here are the key lessons I've learned.

Start with the Monolith

Contrary to popular belief, starting with microservices is often a mistake. A well-structured monolith gives you:

  • Faster development velocity
  • Simpler deployment and debugging
  • Clear understanding of system boundaries

Design for Failure

Every system will fail. Plan for it from day one.

// Implement circuit breakers
class CircuitBreaker {
  private failures = 0;
  private readonly threshold = 5;
  private state: 'closed' | 'open' | 'half-open' = 'closed';

  async execute(fn: () => Promise): Promise {
    if (this.state === 'open') {
      throw new Error('Circuit breaker is open');
    }

    try {
      const result = await fn();
      this.onSuccess();
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      this.onFailure();
      throw error;
    }
  }

  private onSuccess() {
    this.failures = 0;
    this.state = 'closed';
  }

  private onFailure() {
    this.failures++;
    if (this.failures >= this.threshold) {
      this.state = 'open';
      setTimeout(() => this.state = 'half-open', 30000);
    }
  }
}

Observability is Key

You can't fix what you can't see. Invest in:

  • Structured logging
  • Distributed tracing
  • Metrics and dashboards
  • Alerting on key signals

Scale Horizontally

Design your systems to scale out, not up. This means:

  • Stateless services
  • External state stores (databases, caches)
  • Load balancing across instances

Conclusion

Building scalable systems is as much about process and culture as it is about technology. Focus on fundamentals, measure everything, and always be learning.
